subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add a core automatic final-output sanitization boundary for secrets and PII, and exactly which sinks and defaults should it own?
rationale: The security goal is valid, but the scope, defaults, config surface, false-positive tolerance, plugin seams, and interaction with SecretRefs/log redaction need secops/product intent before implementation.

options.title: Define core sanitizer boundary
options.body: Create a secops-approved core boundary that reuses `redactSensitiveText` and the secret registry for final replies and any explicitly selected adjacent sinks, with focused tests and docs.

options.title: Expose extension seams first
options.body: Keep core policy minimal and add only the missing plugin or middleware hooks needed for an official or community sanitizer to own detection and output behavior.

options.title: Document existing mitigations only
options.body: Decline global final-output filtering for now and clarify that SecretRefs, log/transcript redaction, sandboxing, and explicit plugins/skills are the supported mitigations.

recommendation.title: Define core sanitizer boundary
recommendation.body: Create a secops-approved core boundary that reuses `redactSensitiveText` and the secret registry for final replies and any explicitly selected adjacent sinks, with focused tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the CODEOWNERS-routed group for the relevant secrets and security-boundary surfaces.
